SECTION 1
The alarm clock screams its digital decree,
But I pull the covers over my head,
Forgetting the world and its academic plea,
While dreams of naps and soft pillows spread.
The syllabus mocks me from the desk in shame,
A roadmap to a place I won't go,
I whisper lies to justify the game,
"I'll be there next week," is all I know.

SECTION 2
My notebook yawns with empty, white despair,
A canvas blank where knowledge should reside,
While peers take notes with frantic, ink-stained care,
I scroll through feeds with nowhere left to hide.
The group chat buzzes, "Did you catch the part?"
I type a lie and hope the signal holds,
With every absence, panic starts to dart,
A story of neglect that never folds.

SECTION 3
I've built a throne of cushions, soft and deep,
Where I attend the lecture of the TV,
The couch becomes my desk, my vigil keep,
Of all the credits that I'm destined to see.
But tuition dollars drift like autumn leaves,
While I remain rooted here in sloth and gray,
The degree recedes, a promise I believe,
I'll earn someday, if I just find the way.
Yet "someday" waits behind a closed bedroom door,
And attendance records tick with silent score.

SECTION 4
Now guilt and greed collide within my chest,
I paid the fee, I skipped the lecture hall,
I put my education to the test,
And failed it, answering the couch's call.
But wait, a thought arises, wild and bright,
A question bold enough to break the mold,
I'll ask the question with all my might,
And hope the answer isn't what I hold.
I clear my throat, I look the registrar in the eye,
And ask the question, hoping I won't cry:
Can I get my money back for the classes I missed?

The Stack Overflow That Ate My Weekend: A Riddle for the Chronically Debugged

If you’ve spent more than three years in this field, you know that the most dangerous line of code isn’t written in C++, Rust, or even COBOL. It’s the one you wrote at 2:14 p.m. on a Tuesday, convinced you were being clever. Cleverness, as we’ve all learned, is just technical debt wearing a party hat. We spend our days optimizing pipelines, refactoring monoliths, and pretending we understand distributed systems. But beneath the Kubernetes clusters and the microservices lies a fundamental truth: we are all just writing functions that call themselves until something breaks. Today, I’m skipping the usual architecture deep-dive and serving you something far more valuable: a riddle. Not a metaphor. Not a poetic tribute to open source. A proper, old-fashioned, “guess-me-before-you-panic” riddle. Consider it a warm-up for your next stand-up, an icebreaker for your next hackathon, or a gentle reminder that your production environment is watching you.

I begin by calling myself, yet I never truly start.
I carry a base case, though you’ll inevitably forget it in the dark.
I grow without a body, I shrink without a breath.
I’ll segfault your Friday deploy, defying all your death.
I have no memory, yet I remember every step I take.
I’m elegant on paper, but a nightmare in the wake.
What am I?

Let’s break this down for the uninitiated, or perhaps for those of you who are currently sweating through your ergonomic keyboard. The first line is a dead giveaway if you’ve ever read a textbook, but a trap if you’ve ever actually run it. “I begin by calling myself” describes the moment you write a function that invokes its own name. You think you’re being clever. You are not. The second line references the base case, the mathematical equivalent of an exit door. Every recursive function needs one, or it will loop until your laptop fan sounds like a jet engine preparing for takeoff. The third line plays with physical intuition. Recursion doesn’t have a body, yet it grows deeper with every call. It doesn’t breathe, yet it collapses when you finally hit the limit. The fourth line is where the humor turns to trauma. “Segfault your Friday deploy” is not hyperbole. It is a documentary statement. The fifth line nods to the call stack, which remembers everything you’ve done, even when you wish it wouldn’t. The final line captures the universal CS experience: beautiful in theory, catastrophic in practice.

If you guessed recursion, congratulations. You either passed your algorithms midterm or you’ve been burned at least once. If you guessed something else, I respect your confidence, but your stack trace is lying to you.

In all seriousness, this riddle exists because recursion is the perfect microcosm of our profession. We build elegant abstractions, forget the edge cases, and then spend three hours debugging a function that should have terminated in O(1). The next time you write a self-referential function, ask yourself: do I have a base case? Is my termination condition bulletproof? And most importantly, did I test this before the product manager scheduled the demo? Because the stack doesn’t care about your deadlines. It only cares about depth. And depth, much like technical debt, always compounds. After all, every senior engineer was once a junior who thought they understood the call stack. So share this with your team. Print it on a whiteboard. Frame it above your monitor. And when you inevitably hit a stack overflow at 4:58 p.m., remember: you were warned. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have a merge conflict to resolve, and it’s calling itself.

#ComputerScience #Recursion #DebuggingHumor #TechRiddles #StackOverflow #SoftwareEngineering

उद्यमिता के सपने

नया सपना, नया सफर, उद्यम का ज्वार,
विचारों की गंगा से बहे नया संसार।

शिक्षा का द्वार खोलें, ज्ञान का दीप जलाएँ,
ग्राम-ग्राम तक पहुँचाएँ, कौशल की नई राहें।

स्वास्थ्य सेवा की दूरी, दूर करें हर बीमारी,
टेलीचिकित्सा के सहारे, मिले हर घर दवाई।

किसान की मेहनत को, बाज़ार से जोड़ें,
फसल की कीमत निश्चित, उसकी कल को रोशन करें।

प्रकृति की रक्षा करें, पुनर्चक्रण के चक्र,
सौर ऊर्जा के किरणों से, नया युग सजेकर।

डिजिटल वित्त की राह, साधारण जन को सहारा,
कृत्रिम बुद्धि के सहारे, कार्य हों सरल सारा।

स्थानीय हस्तशिल्प को, विश्व तक पहुँचाएँ,
'वंदे गृह निर्मित' की ध्वनि, संसार में गूँजाएँ।

जोखिम लो, हार मत मानो, दृढ़ संकल्प रखो,
नवाचार की मशाल लिए, नया इतिहास रचो।
विचारों से ही जन्म ले, सफलता का वृक्ष उगे,
उद्यमिता के पथ पर चलो, स्वप्न साकार होंगे।
